summary: British casino owner John Aspinall ran illegal high-stakes gambling parties and then the Clermont Club, fleecing London's aristocracy, while his private Kent zoos killed several keepers and he preached eugenic misanthropy.

evidence.note: born in Delhi in 1926 into a colonial family; childhood in India
long segment on the public-school prefect and fagging system, hazing and sexual abuse of boys
early 1950s chemmy parties in rotating private houses begin his gambling fortune
Clermont house players kept games running so the house cut grew while rich marks lost
vivid account of a tiger mauling a visiting child's face in 1970
Aspinall's misanthropic eugenic views, calls to cull humans and admiration for Hitler's eugenics
Clermont set's far-right turn, socialist conspiracy fears and talk of a military coup
Lucan's attempt to kill his wife after trying to have her committed; nanny killed
keeper deaths at his zoos from 1980 to the 1990s; dies of cancer in 2000

notes: No theme for gambling, aristocracy/class or animal keeping; fraud-grift is the closest primary (casino fleecing aristocrats via house players), hence low.
